## Importers

Importers of high-risk AI systems have the following obligations [(Article 23(6-7))]:

- Provide relevant competent authorities, upon reasoned request, with all necessary information and documentation to demonstrate conformity with requirements, including certificates, instructions for use, and EU declarations of conformity, in an easily understood language [(Article 23(6))].
- Ensure technical documentation can be made available to authorities [(Article 23(6))].
- Cooperate with relevant competent authorities in any action they take regarding high-risk AI systems placed on the market by the importers, particularly to reduce and mitigate risks [(Article 23(7))].

## Distributors

Distributors of high-risk AI systems have the following obligations [(Article 24(1-3))]:

- Before making a high-risk AI system available on the market, verify that it bears the required CE marking, is accompanied by an EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, and that the provider and importer have complied with their obligations [(Article 24(1))].
- Not make the system available on the market if it is not in conformity with requirements; inform the provider or importer if the system presents a risk [(Article 24(2))].
- Ensure that storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance with requirements [(Article 24(3))].
- Cooperate with relevant competent authorities in any action they take regarding high-risk AI systems made available by the distributors, particularly to reduce or mitigate risks [(Article 24(6))].

## Deployers

Deployers of high-risk AI systems have the following obligations [(Article 26(1-6))]:

- Take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use systems in accordance with accompanying instructions for use [(Article 26(1))].
- Assign human oversight to natural persons with necessary competence, training, authority, and support [(Article 26(2))].
- Ensure input data is relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose, to the extent the deployer controls input data [(Article 26(4))].
- Monitor operation of the high-risk AI system based on instructions for use and inform providers accordingly; suspend use if the system may present a risk; immediately inform providers and market surveillance authorities of serious incidents [(Article 26(5))].
